skill.name: tdd-workflows-tdd-cycle
skill.description: Guide a disciplined test-driven development cycle from a failing test through implementation, verification, and cleanup.
skill.summary: A practical Red-Green-Refactor workflow for incremental, test-focused development.
skill.author: sickn33

content.value_statement: Unstructured test work can produce oversized changes and unclear failures. This skill guides small Red-Green-Refactor steps that keep implementation and verification aligned.
actual_capabilities: Break a feature into a small testable behavior.
Define a failing test before implementation.
Guide the minimum implementation needed to pass.
Verify test results and investigate failures.
Refactor working code while preserving test coverage.
limitations: It does not run tests or edit the repository by itself.
It does not choose the correct testing framework without project context.
It cannot guarantee complete coverage or correct business requirements.
It does not replace code review, integration testing, or security testing.

use_cases.title: Build a Small Feature
use_cases.description: Use a short Red-Green-Refactor loop to implement one observable behavior with focused tests.

use_cases.title: Fix a Regression
use_cases.description: Reproduce the reported failure with a test, apply the smallest fix, and verify related behavior.

use_cases.title: Improve Test Discipline
use_cases.description: Apply incremental test planning and cleanup practices during pair programming or code review preparation.

prompt_templates.title: Start a TDD Cycle
prompt_templates.prompt: I need to implement [behavior]. Help me define one focused failing test, explain the expected result, and identify the smallest next step.

prompt_templates.title: Implement the Minimum
prompt_templates.prompt: Given this failing test and project context, propose the smallest implementation that makes the test pass. Keep the change limited to [scope].

prompt_templates.title: Review the Cycle
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Red-Green-Refactor cycle. Identify whether the test isolates one behavior, whether the implementation is minimal, and what should be refactored next.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Test Suite Increment
prompt_templates.prompt: For [feature or regression], design an incremental TDD plan across unit and integration boundaries. Order the tests, note dependencies, and define verification points.

output_examples.input: Add validation that rejects an empty project name.
output: Test: an empty name returns a validation error.
Implementation: add the smallest validation branch.
Verification: run the focused test, then the related suite.

output_examples.input: A parser regression accepts a malformed date.
output: Reproduction test: malformed dates are rejected.
Fix: tighten the parser condition without changing valid-date behavior.
Follow-up: run parser tests and review the focused diff.

best_practices: Keep each test focused on one observable behavior.
Make the smallest implementation change that passes the test.
Run focused tests first, then run the related suite before cleanup.
anti_patterns: Writing tests that already pass before the behavior is implemented.
Changing tests to hide a failing implementation.
Combining unrelated behavior changes in one TDD cycle.

faq.question: What development method does this skill use?
faq.answer: It uses the Red-Green-Refactor cycle: write a failing test, implement the behavior, then improve the working code.

faq.question: Can it run my tests?
faq.answer: No. It provides workflow guidance and commands to consider, but your development environment must run the tests.

faq.question: Does it support existing codebases?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide regression tests and incremental changes when existing code has partial or uneven test coverage.

faq.question: Which testing framework should I use?
faq.answer: Use the framework already established by the project. The skill does not require a specific language or testing library.

faq.question: How large should each change be?
faq.answer: Keep each change small enough to explain through one behavior and its focused tests.

faq.question: Does TDD guarantee defect-free code?
faq.answer: No. TDD improves feedback and design discipline, but broader integration, security, performance, and review checks remain necessary.
